summary: Emergency dental treatment in Las Vegas for a missing front tooth
story: I was in Las Vegas from June 19 for a friend's bachelor party. On the morning of June 21 I woke up on the floor of our suite missing an upper front tooth. I have no memory of the night before, and neither do my friends. I am a dentist, and I have to say that the extraction is consistent with my own technique. I went to an emergency dental clinic that morning for an exam, an X-ray and a temporary bridge, and their bill and notes are attached. There was also a tiger in the bathroom of the suite, which I mention only for completeness. I am not claiming for anything connected with the tiger.

documents.name: Clinic invoice
documents.content: Desert Springs Emergency Dental, Las Vegas, June 21, 2026. Patient Stuart Price. Emergency examination: $140.00. Periapical X-ray: $150.00. Temporary bridge, tooth 10: $1,060.00. Total: $1,350.00. Paid by card.

documents.name: Clinical notes
documents.content: Desert Springs Emergency Dental, June 21, 2026, 10:40. Patient Stuart Price, age 47, a dentist. Tooth 10, the upper left lateral incisor, is missing. The socket is clean with a clot in place, consistent with a recent extraction using instruments. The patient believes he removed the tooth himself during the night and has no memory from about 10 pm to 9 am. He and his companions report heavy drinking through the evening of June 20, and he smelled of alcohol and was unsteady on arrival. No other injury. Treatment: exam, X-ray, temporary bridge. Advised to see his own dentist at home. Dr. R. Okafor, DDS.
